reading: The impairment producer refused its own verdict because `noInputReachedTheRoomAfterTheEpisodeClosed` came back false: input reached the room **after** the recovery episode had closed. Its latency bands were inside envelope (baseline intake p99 44.69 ms against imposed intake p50 83.62 ms; client-observed p50 126.64 ms baseline against 188.94 ms imposed), so what moved is post-close containment, not rate. That is the mechanism §3 of the W-A diagnosis hypothesised — a timer or an in-flight message straddling the close — seen in the producer’s own instrumentation rather than in the accepted case. The same production also logged the matchmaking-side refusal text three times ("reconnection token invalid or expired"), which is the branch the accepted P-2b assertion expects, not the seat-reservation branch.
consequences: the producer-gate class is not one assertion: in two consecutive records-only runs it was `mappingMatchesTheAuthoritysOwnRecord` (run 44206639883) and now `noInputReachedTheRoomAfterTheEpisodeClosed`, two accepted producers with two different post-close samples

both failures happened in the **third** of five capture plans, so the job died before the whole-task plan: from now on a red in an earlier plan means the `UDG-003-TASK` bundle simply does not exist that run
no test failed, so a reader who triages by junit alone would conclude nothing happened
